page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.24xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 Graviton processors built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform provisions 96 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, coupled with 384 GB of system RAM at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. High-throughput local storage is bundled directly via 5,700 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps. The instance operates without discrete GPU hardware acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier parallel execution and I/O capacity. Multi-core performance is characterized by top-decile scores in stress-ng multi-core testing (163,541.37) and Geekbench multi-core analysis (25,762.0), reinforced by exceptional Clang software compilation throughput. Memory subsystem testing reflects top-tier bandwidth, delivering 480.63 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 226.58 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database tests, Redis SET transactions (198.92 million operations per second), and static web delivery (149.81 GB/sec) consistently register in the highest performance percentiles. In contrast, single-core metrics sit in the middle 50% band.

The instance delivers high compute and storage density per core, yielding cost-effective multi-threaded throughput for workloads optimized for ARM64 architectures. The physical-to-virtual core parity eliminates hyperthreading contention, though single-threaded computational tasks do not show notable acceleration. Primary workload targets include large-scale key-value datastores, distributed in-memory databases, continuous integration build clusters, and parallel ETL pipelines that leverage local NVMe caching.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.24xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz, 384 GB of memory, and 5,700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage on the Nitro hypervisor. With 4.0 GB of RAM per core and a 40 Gbps baseline network connection, it achieves top-tier results in multi-threaded benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core, Redis SET operations, and PassMark database processing. Large-block memory bandwidth exceeds 480 GB/sec for reads, reflecting superior data throughput. Single-core performance falls within average ranges, and the instance omits GPU accelerators. The hardware configuration delivers high resource density and execution stability for I/O-intensive workloads, distributed caching tiers, large-scale software compilation, and high-concurrency database deployments.
